newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab confirms asked to join plane project.
newsitem.headline: Saab confirms asked to join plane project.

text.p: Swedish aircraft group Saab Aircraft on Wednesday confirmed a newspaper report saying it was invited by the European aircraft group Aero International (Regional) to participate in developing a regional plane.
"Yes, that is the case. There is little to add. It is an invitation to discussions and then we will have to see what happens," Saab Aircraft's spokesman Lars Jagerfelt told Reuters.

The AI(R) consortium consists of British Aerospace and ATR, owned by France's Aerospatiale and Italy's Alenia. AI(R) is considering producing a 70 seat jet plane for regional airlines and has invited Saab Aircraft to help develope it.
Saab Aircraft has also been invited by Airbus to help develop the super jumbo A3XX. Airbus wants Saab Aircraft to account for five percent of the development costs.
Saab Aircraft is wholly owned by Swedish Investor AB, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire.
